text: In 2024, property taxes went up in 91 of Iowa's 99 counties. Families are paying more, and they deserve to know every dollar is spent well.

text: But three out of four Iowa towns have fewer than 2,500 people and no financial analyst. In one county, $127,000 in duplicate payments went unnoticed for three years.

speaker: david
picture: BUBBLE over slide "Who it's for": three cards slide in (City clerks · Councils · Taxpayers)
text: Red Pen reads every payment a city makes and marks only the ones a person should review. It's built for city clerks, finance officers, and councils in small towns that can't afford an auditor on staff.

speaker: alex
picture: BUBBLE: the town's spending export in a spreadsheet (Check Date, Payee Name, Net Amount, 1,885 rows), the file flies into Red Pen's upload box, the import summary appears
text: A clerk starts by dropping in the city's spending file, exported straight from their accounting software. Here's five years of books from our test town.

speaker: srihari
picture: BUBBLE: reading animation, zoom to "1,885 transactions read. 20 need you." Pop-up: *1,885 read · 20 flagged · 1 second*
text: In about a second, Red Pen reads all 1,885 payments and finds 20 worth a look. Every finding explains itself in plain English.

speaker: alex
picture: BUBBLE: opens the duplicate payment, zooms on the reasons (pop-up *$4,645 × 2 · 12 days apart*), types a note, clicks Mark reviewed
text: This janitorial invoice was paid twice, twelve days apart. The clerk checks the numbers, adds a note, and marks it reviewed, and the decision goes into an audit log. Red Pen never blocks a payment. People decide.

speaker: srihari
picture: BUBBLE: Vendors (pop-up *Bobs Plumbing = Bob's Plumbing Service*), Spending patterns (July snow bill circled), Budget runway (pop-up *Runs out: April*)
text: It catches what a spreadsheet misses: the same plumber under two spellings, a snow-removal bill in July, and a fire-truck repair budget on track to run out in April.

speaker: alex
picture: BUBBLE: Contracts view, red underlines and margin notes appear
text: And before the council signs a contract, it underlines risky terms, like automatic renewal with no new bid.

speaker: srihari
picture: BUBBLE over slide "How it works": spending file → four models + Iowa State Auditor rules → plain-English findings → a person decides. Each model's name pops in as it's said
text: Under the hood are four models we wrote from scratch in JavaScript, with no machine-learning libraries: an Isolation Forest for unusual payments, gradient-boosted trees that learn each month's normal spending, a seasonal ARIMA forecast for budgets, and a naive Bayes classifier for contracts.

speaker: david
picture: BUBBLE: the real source code in a VS Code-style editor, scrolling `isolationForest.js`
text: Every flag still comes with a reason a clerk can check by hand.

speaker: alex
picture: BUBBLE: a browser window with a lock icon; pop-up *No server · data stays on your computer*
text: It all runs in the browser, so a city's data never leaves its computer.

speaker: david
picture: BUBBLE: the 10-of-10 checklist ticks down, then a terminal runs the real test suite: *35 pass, 0 fail*
text: To test it honestly, we planted ten real-world problems in our test town's books. Red Pen caught all ten, and 35 automated tests check the code.

speaker: srihari
picture: BUBBLE over the closing slide: parks, roads, schools icons; recap *1,885 read · 20 flagged · 10 of 10 caught*
text: Every dollar a small town saves stays in its parks, its roads, and its schools, instead of coming out of higher property taxes.
